solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Minister's secret token of bargain with God

definitions.note: read as 'Minister is', the 's linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: the Lord is God
privy means private or secret, as in 'privy to'
a seal is the token set on an agreement to confirm it

explanation.surface: A politician's covert pact with the Almighty, sealed with some token.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lord Privy Seal is one of the great officers of state in the UK government, nowadays usually a cabinet minister without a department.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a senior post in the British cabinet held by a government minister.

clue.text: Short communication about a junior cleaner

indicators.note: the shortened word goes around the rest, enclosing it
short means the word is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: a letter is a written communication
taken as written
a junior is under someone else, lower in rank

explanation.surface: A brief note concerning a young cleaning assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junior cleaner' looks like one phrase for a trainee; 'junior' belongs to the wordplay and 'cleaner' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A launderette is a self-service laundry, a place that cleans clothes, so loosely a cleaner.

clue.text: Capital love letter read out

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
love is nil in tennis, the shape of an O

explanation.surface: A love letter recited from the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: In the NATO phonetic alphabet, used when letters are spoken over radio, Romeo stands for R. 'Love letter' wants to be one phrase; the words split after 'love'.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo is the code word spoken for the letter R in the radio alphabet.

clue.text: Lawman almost leaving car with boy

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: parking is leaving a car in a spot
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A law officer nearly abandoning his vehicle with a lad.
explanation.walkthrough: C. Northcote Parkinson coined Parkinson's Law: work expands to fill the time available. 'Lawman' suggests a sheriff, but it is the man behind a law.
explanation.definitionFit: Parkinson is the author of the famous satirical law named after him, so he is a man known for a law.

clue.text: Rowena's husband in one front garden

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
the van is the front, as in vanguard
to hoe is to work a garden, a verb here

explanation.surface: A woman's husband standing in the front garden.
explanation.walkthrough: In Walter Scott's novel Ivanhoe, the hero marries the Saxon lady Rowena.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilfred of Ivanhoe, title knight of Scott's novel, weds Rowena at its close.

clue.text: Longing to tour Middle East country

indicators.note: touring means going all around, so the longing surrounds the region

parts.note: a yen is a longing or craving

explanation.surface: A yearning to travel around a Middle Eastern nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Yemen is a nation at the southern tip of the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Badly spoiled one line in solid figure

indicators.note: badly means these letters are set wrong and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something badly ruined, set inside a three-dimensional shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipsoid is a three-dimensional shape whose cross-sections are ellipses, like a stretched sphere.

clue.text: Cut and run? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls one letter short of complete

parts.note: to lope is to run with long easy strides

explanation.surface: A cut-and-run escape that does not quite come off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut and run' reads as one idiom for fleeing; 'Cut' is the definition and 'run' the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To lop is to cut off, as with branches from a tree.

clue.text: Island battle from two months back

indicators.note: back means the letters are read in the other direction

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for month, and AUG for August

explanation.surface: A wartime island fight dating from two months previously.
explanation.walkthrough: Guam, a Pacific island, gave its name to a 1944 battle, so both senses fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Guam is a Pacific island and the site of a major Second World War battle.

clue.text: Let me make this clear: you don't have to listen

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an emphatic phrase insisting that the speaker means it
second meaning: a literal instruction to lip-read rather than hear

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase, famous from George Bush senior's 'no new taxes', is emphatic; taken literally, it invites lip-reading, so no ears are needed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom insists on being taken seriously, while its literal sense asks someone to watch the speaker's mouth.

clue.text: Without energy, a devil is hard to reprove

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: without means the energy is dropped from the devil

parts.note: a demon is a devil
taken as written

explanation.surface: A demon with no energy is tough to scold.
explanation.definitionFit: To admonish is to warn or rebuke someone mildly, the same as reproving them.

clue.text: Linen putting lines on back of neck

indicators.note: in an across clue, putting lines on something places them after it

parts.note: the nape is the back of the neck
RY, short for railway, stands for lines of track

explanation.surface: Putting a strip of linen around the back of one's neck.
explanation.definitionFit: Napery is an old word for household linen, especially table napkins and cloths.

clue.text: Litter replaced with worse pups perhaps

indicators.note: replaced means the letters are put back in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A litter swapped for worse puppies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' seems to be the definition for pups; it is anagram fodder instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Rottweilers are a dog breed, so their young are examples of pups.

clue.text: In one drop, rain oddly glittering

indicators.note: in places the odd letters inside the other pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a descent is a drop or fall

indicators.note: oddly means take the first, third and later odd-numbered letters of the word rain

parts.note: the word rain supplies its first and third letters

explanation.surface: A single falling raindrop, sparkling strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iridescent shows shimmering rainbow colours, as a sparkling surface does.

clue.text: Unequivocal, in writing with one hand

parts.note: to put something down is to set it in writing
right is one hand, the other being left

explanation.surface: Something made plain in a letter penned with a single hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright means absolute or plain-spoken, leaving no doubt, as unequivocal does.

clue.text: Ditch worker perhaps is cutting

parts.note: a trench is a ditch
a worker is one kind of ant, so an ant is an example

explanation.surface: A labourer digging a ditch is cutting through earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditch worker' reads as a navvy; the words split into a ditch and an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant remarks are incisive and sharp, so cutting in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Crop farm animals initially ignored

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is dropped, so the beginning is ignored

parts.note: goats are farm animals

explanation.surface: Livestock at first paid no attention to the harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats are a cereal grown as a field crop.

clue.text: Not a way for waiter to produce dish of meat

indicators.note: not means those letters are left out of the waiter

parts.note: a steward waits on passengers, as on a ship or plane
taken as written
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A waiter has no route for bringing out a meat course.
explanation.definitionFit: A stew is a dish of meat slowly simmered in liquid.

clue.text: Forced to agree with dandelion being uprooted

indicators.note: uprooted means the letters are pulled up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Made to consent, along with a dandelion pulled up from the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone nailed down has been pinned to a firm commitment, made to agree definitely.

clue.text: Quite unemotional senior detective about to arrest Green and Liberal

indicators.note: arresting means holding the other pieces inside
about means the detective's letters turn round

parts.note: DCI is Detective Chief Inspector, a senior British police rank
eco- describes green, environmental things

explanation.surface: A cool senior policeman about to arrest a Green and a Liberal politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice-cold describes someone completely without feeling, utterly calm and detached.

clue.text: This system gives compiler no end of artifice

parts.note: the compiler is the setter, who says me

indicators.note: the final letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a trick is an artifice

explanation.surface: A system that gives the setter endless ingenuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' looks like 'plenty of'; here it docks a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The metric system is the decimal system of measurement, so it names a system.

clue.text: African country stopping short a line of dancers

indicators.note: stopping short means the country's last letter is dropped

parts.note: Congo is an African country
taken as written

explanation.surface: An African nation halting a dance line abruptly.
explanation.definitionFit: A conga is a Latin American dance done in a long single-file line.

clue.text: Sets about leaving OT book in assembly

indicators.note: leaving means those letters depart from the book's name

parts.note: Ecclesiastes is a book of the Old Testament

indicators.note: about means the word sets is turned round

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: Groups about to leave a biblical book during a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecclesia is a Greek word for a gathering, the assembly of citizens in ancient Athens or a church congregation.

clue.text: Impatient to turn up half-hearted rhythmic music

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading the letters bottom to top
half-hearted means one of the two central letters is lost

parts.note: reggae is a rhythmic Jamaican style of music

explanation.surface: Keen to switch on some lacklustre dance music.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of this music is a double letter; losing half of it drops just one.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager means keen and impatient to do something.

clue.text: Formidable woman writer, one with blue veins

parts.note: a gorgon is a fearsome woman, after the snake-haired monsters of Greek myth
Emile Zola was a French novelist

explanation.surface: A daunting female author with blue veins showing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One with blue veins' seems to describe the formidable woman; it describes a cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorgonzola is an Italian cheese marbled with blue mould running through it.

clue.text: Yob partial to a fight

indicators.note: partial means only part of the following words, to a fight, is taken

parts.note: the answer sits across the end of to, the word a and the start of fight

explanation.surface: A thug who is fond of a scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partial to' reads as 'fond of'; it signals a part of the next words. A yob is a British word for a loutish youth.
explanation.definitionFit: An oaf is a clumsy lout, much like a yob, a British slang word for a hooligan.

clue.text: A feature of Scotland: golf course with eagles?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a narrow Scottish valley
second meaning: add eagles to it and you have Gleneagles, the famous Scottish golf course

explanation.walkthrough: Gleneagles is a golf resort in Perthshire; an eagle in golf is two under par, so 'with eagles' sounds like a golfing score.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow valley, typical of Scottish landscape, and it begins the name of a celebrated course.

clue.text: Irregular activity from sex workers on suitable beaches

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the following pieces

parts.note: fit means suitable
sands are beaches
tarts is slang for prostitutes

explanation.surface: Prostitutes plying their trade along the right beaches.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things by fits and starts means working spasmodically, in bursts, not steadily.
